kids.name: impact (§8.2)
impact · bybit
kids.chars: Bybit is not affected: the restore doesn't touch your positions or orders there. They stay live on Bybit while CandleViewer restores, so resting orders can fill and stops can trigger.

kids.name: impact · rewind
kids.chars: This rewinds CandleViewer's own records (users, settings, orders as recorded, audit) to the backup taken at 2026-10-21 01:00 UTC. Anything recorded after it is replaced, except what the security section below says.

kids.name: impact · config
kids.chars: Server settings go back to the backup's copy too (service files, database settings, start-up scripts); a setting changed since is lost.

kids.name: impact · trading
kids.chars: Trading is switched off during the restore and stays off until you turn it back on.

kids.name: impact · reconcile
kids.chars: Before you can, CandleViewer re-reads Bybit; anything it no longer recognises is listed for you to review.

kids.name: impact · market
kids.chars: Market history is not restored from these backups.

kids.name: impact · secrets
kids.chars: API keys go back to the backup's copy, still encrypted; they work only on a server that holds the same master key. Keys revoked since are in the security section.

kids.name: impact · signin
kids.chars: Sign-in goes back too: afterwards, you and your users sign in with the passwords and two-factor apps you had on 2026-10-21.

kids.name: impact · security_today
kids.chars: The server may refuse a restore that would roll back security changes made after this backup.

kids.name: restore.impact.audit
kids.chars: The audit log goes back to this backup too; this restore's record is kept outside the database and added back.

kids.note: §8.2's copy only; nothing says 'safe', 'undo' or 'recover your trades' (RES:780-784)

Every figure's accessible name carries its unit in words ("820 megabytes", "210 milliseconds", "48 percent", "60 frames per second, 95th-percentile frame time 12 milliseconds", "2 chain trips", "step 3 of 8"); the visible text keeps the short form, and an age carries its absolute UTC time in its description (D02:119).
